hints: Focus on the fact that propan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, so oxidation happens in two stages with the aldehyde in the middle.
Notice that propanal has a much lower boiling point than propan-1-ol and propanoic acid, so it can be boiled off easily as soon as it forms.
Think about which apparatus removes the volatile product from the oxidising agent straight away, and which apparatus keeps everything together for further reaction.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the two-stage oxidation**

Remember that a primary alcohol is oxidised first to an aldehyde, then to a carboxylic acid if oxidation continues.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$$

**See the problem to solve**

Reaction 2 is the first step to make propanal. Reaction 1 is the full oxidation to propanoic acid.

To stop at propanal, we must remove it from the acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ as soon as it forms, before it can be oxidised again.

**Choose distillation over reflux**

Propanal boils at about $49^{\circ}\text{C}$, much lower than propan-1-ol and propanoic acid, so gentle warming lets it distil off immediately.

Distillation collects the aldehyde away from the oxidant, while heating under reflux would return it to the flask and allow full oxidation to the acid.

options.A: Excess oxidising agent does the opposite of what we want. More $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ ensures plenty of [O] is available, so any propanal formed is quickly oxidised further to propanoic acid.
options.B: Dilute sulfuric acid is needed to acidify the dichromate, but adding excess concentrated acid does not stop the second oxidation step. It does not remove propanal from the mixture.
options.C: Immediate distillation is correct. Propanal is distilled off as soon as it forms because of its low boiling point, so it leaves the flask and cannot stay in contact with the oxidant to form propanoic acid.
options.D: Heating under reflux keeps all vapours condensed and returned to the flask. This keeps propanal in prolonged contact with hot oxidant, so it is further oxidised to propanoic acid (reaction 1).
